mainTopic: The sources that a כהן lacking or misusing his garments (מחוסר בגדים) or a כהן who drank wine (שתויי יין) disqualifies the עבודה, and which garment problems disqualify.
overview: The גמרא is looking for the source that a כהן serving without his proper garments (מחוסר בגדים) ruins the עבודה. A ברייתא links מחוסר בגדים, שתויי יין and unwashed hands and feet through the shared word "חוקה", but that link alone would cover only rites for which a זר is חייב מיתה. So a separate פסוק is needed to cover every rite. שתויי יין then borrows that full rule back from מחוסר בגדים through the same link. The פסוק "ולהבדיל" was the source only before the link was set up. Its lasting job is to teach that someone who drank wine should not give rulings, as רב practiced on יום טוב. The גמרא then shows why two more פסוקים are still needed. "ונתנו" adds rites that are not required for כפרה, and "וערכו" adds wearing extra garments, not just missing ones. Finally a ברייתא lists practical garment problems: garments that drag, are too short or are frayed are still כשר. A second list of cases begins, and its ruling comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא's link through the word "statute"
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the challenge from before: a ברייתא already links שתויי יין, the garments and washing through the word "חוקה", so why does מחוסר בגדים need its own פסוק?
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says "statute" here and "statute" there, which creates a גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא that links several cases through the shared word "חוקה". This is the end of a challenge to the source just given for מחוסר בגדים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "חוקה" appears for שתויי יין, for the כהן's garments, and for washing hands and feet. A גזירה שוה teaches that the rule in one place applies to the others. If so, the rule for מחוסר בגדים seems to come from here already, and the separate פסוק looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (it comes to say)
Statute; the shared word that creates the link
A teaching that links two places in the תורה by a shared word

phrases.english: The verse states: "statute" and "statute"
phrases.notes: The word 'statute' appears for wine drinkers and also for the garments (שמות 28:43) and washing (שמות 30:21).

phrases.english: for a verbal analogy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge, begun earlier on the דף, against the separate פסוק for מחוסר בגדים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a special פסוק to teach that a מחוסר בגדים disqualifies the עבודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's גזירה שוה of "חוקה" already gives this rule, so the פסוק seems extra.

steps.title: The analogy alone would be too narrow
steps.stepSummary: From the גזירה שוה alone, we would limit the rule to rites for which a זר is חייב מיתה. The פסוק teaches that it covers every rite.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had that source, I would say: this applies only to a rite for which a non-כהן is liable to death. But a rite for which a non-כהן is not liable to death, I would say no. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Without the separate פסוק, we would have applied the rule of מחוסר בגדים too narrowly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The passage about שתויי יין speaks of rites tied to death ("ולא תמותו"). The ones it covers are rites for which a זר who does them is חייב מיתה. A גזירה שוה carries over only what is in its source, so it would be limited to those rites. The separate פסוק extends the rule for מחוסר בגדים to every rite.

keyTerms.meaning: If it were only from there
I would have thought
A non-כהן
Liable to death (here, at the hand of Heaven)
It teaches us (that this is not so)

phrases.english: If from there, I would say:
this applies only to a rite
for which a non-priest is liable to death,
but a rite for which a non-priest is not
liable to death, I would say not;
so it teaches us.
phrases.notes: It means the separate פסוק about the garments, which covers every rite.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope: the גזירה שוה alone would teach too little.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only rites for which a זר is חייב מיתה would be ruined by a מחוסר בגדים.
steps.terutzMaskana: A מחוסר בגדים disqualifies every rite, as the separate פסוק teaches.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key rule of a גזירה שוה: it carries over the scope of its source, so it may need another פסוק to widen it.

steps.title: What about the wine drinker for all rites?
steps.stepSummary: We now know a מחוסר בגדים ruins every rite. Where do we learn the same full scope for שתויי יין?
steps.simpleTranslation: We found this for one lacking garments. For those who drank wine, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. The full rule is known for מחוסר בגדים, but not yet for שתויי יין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The passage about שתויי יין itself covers only rites for which a זר is חייב מיתה. The wider rule, covering even other rites, was taught only for the garments. So the גמרא needs a source to stretch the rule of שתויי יין to all rites.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found
A כהן lacking his required garments
כהנים who drank wine
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: We have found it for one lacking garments,
those who drank wine, from where do we know?
phrases.notes: The question is about rites for which a זר is not liable to death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן מְחוּסַּר בְּגָדִים, שְׁתוּיֵי יַיִן מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 2's result and asks about the parallel case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that שתויי יין disqualify even rites for which a זר is not חייב מיתה.

steps.title: Borrowing back from the garments
steps.stepSummary: The same "חוקה"–"חוקה" link now runs the other way, from מחוסר בגדים to שתויי יין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes from "statute" and "statute", learned from one lacking garments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שתויי יין learns the full rule from מחוסר בגדים, using the same גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the separate פסוק widened the rule for the garments to every rite, the גזירה שוה can carry that wider rule back to שתויי יין. Now both cases cover all rites.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes (is learned)

steps.whatToRemember: Both מחוסר בגדים and שתויי יין disqualify every rite. The פסוק widens the garments rule, and the "חוקה" link brings it to wine.

phrases.english: It comes from "statute" and "statute"
from one lacking garments.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The גזירה שוה of "חוקה" carries the wide rule from מחוסר בגדים over to שתויי יין.

steps.title: But the ברייתא uses a different verse
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's תנא learns the rule of שתויי יין from "ולהבדיל בין הקדש ובין החול", not from the גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תנא takes it from "That you may put difference between..."!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer. The ברייתא seems to use a different פסוק for שתויי יין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שתויי יין learns from מחוסר בגדים through "חוקה", why does the תנא quote "ולהבדיל" as the source? This suggests the גזירה שוה is not the real source.

keyTerms.meaning: But the תנא (teacher of the ברייתא)
And to separate (ויקרא 10:10)
He takes it (learns it) from

phrases.english: But the tanna
takes it from "That you may put difference between, etc."!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תַּנָּא ״וּלְהַבְדִּיל בֵּין וְגוֹ׳״ קָא נָסֵיב לַהּ
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שתויי יין learns its rule from the גזירה שוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא names "ולהבדיל" as the source, not "חוקה".

steps.title: That was before the analogy was set up
steps.stepSummary: The תנא used "ולהבדיל" only before the גזירה שוה was established. After that, the גזירה שוה is the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: That was before the גזירה שוה stood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תנא spoke at an earlier stage, before the "חוקה" link was worked out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "ולהבדיל" was the source only until the גזירה שוה was in place. Once it was set up, the גזירה שוה became the source for שתויי יין as well, so there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Before
That it stands (is established)

steps.whatToRemember: "ולהבדיל" served as the source only before the גזירה שוה. In the end, the "חוקה" link covers שתויי יין too.

phrases.english: Before the verbal analogy stands.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Timing: the ברייתא's source belongs to the stage before the גזירה שוה was set up.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the ברייתא quotes "ולהבדיל", the גזירה שוה cannot be the source for שתויי יין.
steps.terutzMaskana: "ולהבדיל" was used before the גזירה שוה. Afterward, the גזירה שוה is the source.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to learn in the opposite direction
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's תנא seems to learn מחוסר בגדים from שתויי יין, which is the reverse of what we just said.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תנא learns the rule of מחוסר בגדים from שתויי יין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the direction of the גזירה שוה given in step 4 and relied on in step 6. The ברייתא seems to treat שתויי יין as the source and מחוסר בגדים as the one learning from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said the גזירה שוה teaches שתויי יין from מחוסר בגדים. The ברייתא's wording seems to go the other way. If the direction is reversed, the earlier explanation does not fit the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of the ברייתא
Learns, derives
A כהן missing his required vestments

phrases.english: But the תנא, one lacking vestments
is what he derives from those who drank wine!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תַּנָּא מְחוּסַּר בְּגָדִים הוּא דְּקָא יָלֵיף מִשְּׁתוּיֵי יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the direction of the גזירה שוה given in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the גזירה שוה runs from מחוסר בגדים to שתויי יין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא appears to use שתויי יין as the source, which is the opposite direction

steps.title: Rereading the ברייתא: all three cases are equal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means that מחוסר בגדים, שתויי יין, and one with unwashed hands and feet all follow the same rule, through the גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: from where do we know there is no difference between one lacking vestments, those who drank wine, and one with unwashed hands and feet? The פסוק says 'חוקה'–'חוקה' for a גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by explaining what the תנא really meant. He was not reversing the direction. He was saying that all three cases are treated the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is read as a statement that all three cases are equal, not as a statement about which one is the source. So it no longer contradicts step 4, where שתויי יין learns its full rule from מחוסר בגדים.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means
That there is no difference between them
One who did not wash his hands and feet
Learning one law from another through a shared word

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
From where do we know that there is no distinction
between one lacking vestments and those who drank wine
and one whose hands and feet are not washed?
The verse states: 'statute,' 'statute,'
for a verbal analogy.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא learns מחוסר בגדים from שתויי יין
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא is teaching that all three cases are equal, through the חוקה–חוקה גזירה שוה

steps.title: So why do we need 'ולהבדיל'?
steps.stepSummary: If שתויי יין is learned from the גזירה שוה, the פסוק 'ולהבדיל' seems to have no job.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then why do I need 'ולהבדיל'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the גזירה שוה is the source for שתויי יין, the גמרא asks what the פסוק 'ולהבדיל' teaches. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every פסוק should teach something. If the גזירה שוה already covers שתויי יין, then 'ולהבדיל' needs a different purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it?
To distinguish (ויקרא 10:10)

phrases.english: But why do I need 'to distinguish'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the conclusion that the גזירה שוה is the source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the פסוק 'ולהבדיל' teaches, if not the rule of שתויי יין in the עבודה

steps.title: 'ולהבדיל' teaches רב's practice about drinking and teaching
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק supports רב's practice of not teaching publicly after drinking wine on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for רב's practice: רב would not set up an interpreter to speak for him from one יום טוב day to the next, because of drunkenness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'ולהבדיל' teaches something else: a person who drank wine should not give rulings. רב kept this when he drank on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is moved from עבודה to teaching and ruling. רב did not give public lectures after drinking wine on יום טוב, and the פסוק is the basis for that.

keyTerms.meaning: The speaker who repeated a sage's lecture out loud to the crowd
Drunkenness
יום טוב

phrases.english: For the practice of רב:
for רב would not set up an interpreter over him
phrases.notes: In other words, he would not give a public lecture.

phrases.english: from one יום טוב day to the next,
because of drunkenness.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ולהבדיל' teaches that one who drank wine should not rule or teach, as רב practiced

steps.title: מחוסר בגדים is already learned from another פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The rule of מחוסר בגדים is already taught by 'ונתנו בני אהרן הכהן', so why learn it from here?
steps.simpleTranslation: Still, is it learned from here? It is learned from there: 'And the sons of אהרן the כהן shall put', meaning while in his כהונה. This teaches that a כהן גדול who wore the clothes of a regular כהן and did the עבודה has invalid עבודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the source for מחוסר בגדים itself. Another פסוק already teaches that a כהן without his proper clothes has invalid עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'הכהן' is read as 'בכיהונו', meaning while dressed as a כהן. That already disqualifies a כהן גדול serving in a regular כהן's clothes. So the earlier source looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Still, yet
In his priestly state, wearing his priestly clothes
A regular כהן
His service is invalid

phrases.english: Still, is it derived from here?!
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the source used earlier for מחוסר בגדים, the פסוק about the כהנים's clothing (שמות 29:9).

phrases.english: It is derived from there:
'And the sons of אהרן the כהן shall put'
in his priestly state;
it teaches about a כהן גדול
who wore the vestments of a regular כהן and served,
that his service is invalid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to question the base source for מחוסר בגדים
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the earlier source of מחוסר בגדים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different פסוק ('ונתנו בני אהרן הכהן') already teaches the rule, so the earlier source would add nothing

steps.title: Why 'ונתנו' is still needed: rites not required for atonement
steps.stepSummary: From the earlier source (שמות 29:9) alone, we might limit the rule to rites that are required for atonement. 'ונתנו', which is about putting fire on the מזבח, teaches that even rites not required for atonement are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: If only from there, I would have said: this applies to a rite that holds back atonement. But a rite that does not hold back atonement, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that with only the earlier source, we would apply the rule just to rites required for כפרה. 'ונתנו' is needed to cover the other rites too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only the earlier source, one might think the clothing rule applies only to rites without which there is no כפרה. 'ונתנו' speaks about putting fire on the מזבח, which is not required for כפרה. So it shows the rule covers even those rites, and each source has its own job.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought
Holds back atonement; without it there is no כפרה

steps.whatToRemember: Each source has its own job. The גזירה שוה is the source for שתויי יין in the עבודה. 'ולהבדיל' teaches that one who drank should not rule. 'ונתנו' is needed so the garments rule covers even rites not required for כפרה.

phrases.english: If from there, I would have said:
this applies to a rite that is required for atonement,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל עֲבוֹדָה דְּלָא מְעַכְּבָא כַּפָּרָה – לָא.
phrases.english: but a rite that is not required for atonement, no.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the other source would be too limited
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the earlier source alone, only rites that are required for atonement would be ruined by missing vestments
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ונתנו' (ויקרא 1:7) is needed so that rites not required for atonement are included too

steps.title: Another verse already teaches the garment rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: the rule that a כהן serving in the wrong garments is פסול is already learned from 'וערכו בני אהרן הכהנים', so why learn it from here?
steps.simpleTranslation: But is this rule really learned from here? It is learned from there: 'And the sons of אהרן, the כהנים, shall lay out the pieces.' The word 'הכהנים' means 'in their כהונה.' From here we learn that a כהן הדיוט who wore the garments of a כהן גדול and served, his service is פסולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, different פסוק that seems to already teach the garment rule. If so, our source looks unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11 the challenge came from 'ונתנו בני אהרן הכהן.' Now a new פסוק is brought: the extra word 'הכהנים' in 'וערכו' teaches 'בכיהונן', meaning they must serve dressed as proper כהנים. That source covers a כהן הדיוט wearing the garments of a כהן גדול, so the question is why our source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: But still / and yet (opens another challenge)
In their priestly state (dressed as proper כהנים)
An ordinary כהן (not the כהן גדול)
The eight garments of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: But still, is it derived from here?!
It is derived from there:
"And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall lay out
the pieces, etc."
"The priests" means in their priestly state;
from here we learn regarding an ordinary priest
who wore the garments of the High Priest
and served: his service is disqualified!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 12 defended our source against 'ונתנו', the גמרא raises a second competing source, 'וערכו'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the earlier sources (שמות 29:9 and 'ונתנו') to teach the rule of wrong garments.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'הכהנים בכיהונן' already teaches that serving in the wrong garments is פסול, our source has no job.

steps.title: The earlier sources alone would cover only missing garments
steps.stepSummary: From the earlier sources alone we might think the rule applies only to a lack of garments, not to extra garments. 'וערכו', which speaks of a כהן הדיוט wearing the garments of a כהן גדול, teaches that extra garments also disqualify.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we had only those earlier sources, I would have said this applies only to missing garments, but not to extra garments. So 'וערכו' teaches us that extra garments also disqualify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both are needed. The earlier sources teach missing garments, and 'וערכו' adds the case of wearing too many garments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer splits the rule into two kinds: חיסור (missing garments) and ייתור (extra garments). A כהן גדול in a regular כהן's garments is missing garments, and the earlier sources could be limited to חיסור. 'וערכו' speaks of a כהן הדיוט in the כהן גדול's garments, so it shows that ייתור also makes the עבודה פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Lack: wearing fewer garments than required
Excess: wearing more garments than required
I would have said (a mistaken first thought)
It teaches us (the source is needed for this point)

steps.whatToRemember: Both missing garments (חיסור) and extra garments (ייתור) make a כהן's עבודה פסולה. Each source has its own job.

phrases.english: If it were only from there, I would have said:
this applies only to a lack of garments,
but an excess of garments, no;
so it teaches us otherwise.
phrases.notes: 'It' means 'וערכו' (ויקרא 1:8), whose case is a regular כהן wearing the extra garments of the כהן גדול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by showing what our source adds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source teaches a different case (lack vs. excess), so neither is extra.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the earlier sources alone, only missing garments would disqualify.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'וערכו' (ויקרא 1:8) teaches that extra garments also disqualify the עבודה.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists garment problems that do and do not disqualify
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that garments that drag, are too short, or are frayed do not disqualify the עבודה. It then begins a second list: two pairs of trousers, two belts, a missing or extra garment, a bandage under the garment, and more.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If the garments were dragging on the ground, raised high above it, or frayed, and he served, his service is valid. If he wore two pairs of trousers, two belts, was missing one garment, wore one extra, or had a bandage on a wound under his garment, or if the garments were...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with practical cases about the כהן's garments. The first group is valid; a second group begins, and its ruling comes right after this text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Garments that are too long, too short, or worn out are still proper garments, so the עבודה is כשרה. The second list deals with real changes: doubled garments, a missing or extra garment, or a bandage that separates the garment from the body. It connects to what we just learned about חיסור and ייתור.

keyTerms.meaning: Dragging (garments too long, trailing on the ground)
Raised up (garments too short)
Frayed or worn out
Trousers (one of the כהן's garments)
Belt (one of the כהן's garments)
A bandage or plaster on a wound

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the second list is valid like the first. The ברייתא switches to a new group of cases, and its ruling comes after the list ends.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If the garments were dragging, raised up, or frayed,
and he served, his service is valid.
If he wore two pairs of trousers or two belts,
was lacking one garment, or wore one extra,
or he had a bandage
on a wound on his body under his garment,
or if the garments were…

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיוּ מְרוּשָּׁלִין, מְסוּלָּקִין, מְשׁוּחָקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that lacking or extra garments disqualify, the גמרא brings a ברייתא with practical cases of garment problems.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Garments that are too long, too short, or frayed do not disqualify the עבודה. A second list of cases (doubled garments, missing or extra garments, a bandage under the garment, and more) begins, with its ruling following.
